Code 30/5/2. 24 page images: idx 0 bilingual cover (announces 23 printed pages; last folio reads 24), idx 1 Hindi instructions, idx 2 English General Instructions; English on every even index 2-22, Hindi on every odd index 3-21 (each the Hindi of the page after it). Odd pages checked on the contact sheet, all Hindi; idx 21 confirmed at full size (Hindi Q38 parts). Every English page ends on a whole question or on a printed OR, except idx 20, whose Q38 passage continues on English idx 22; nothing spills onto an odd top. idx 23 (folio 24) is BLANK. General Instructions (i)-(x) confirm full80. Instruction (viii) prints 2 internal choices in B, 2 in C, 2 in D and 3 (of 2 marks) in E: Q22, Q25, Q26, Q29, Q34, Q35, Q36(iii), Q37(iii), Q38(iii), all nine found, and the marking scheme for 30/5/2 walked page by page shows a bare OR at exactly these nine and nowhere else. Section-A keys read off the marking scheme for 30/5/2 and each re-derived: all 20 agree. No keyless voids. Decimal points are ORDINARY full stops on this paper. Sibling of 30/5/1: 41 rows are the same questions (stem, context and options copied byte for byte from 2026-30-5-1 after reading each on this paper's page); 12 rows are new to this set: Q3, Q6, Q11, Q15, Q22(a), Q22(b), Q23, Q28, Q31, Q32, Q35(a), Q35(b). Only difference noticed among the shared ones is the A-R instruction, which this paper opens with 'Directions :' under an '(Assertion and Reason Based Questions)' heading (a stock instruction line; reference context kept). The case studies print no 'Case Study - N' label, so no _caseStudyLabel.

questions.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
questions.subtopic: Consistency from the Ratios of Coefficients
questions.context: Questions number 19 and 20 are Assertion and Reason based questions. Two statements are given, one labelled Assertion (A) and the other labelled Reason (R). Select the correct answer from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below :
questions.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The system of linear equations \(3x - 5y + 7 = 0\) and \(-6x + 10y + 14 = 0\) is inconsistent.

**Reason (R) :** When two linear equations don't have unique solution, they always represent parallel lines.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions._figure: REQUIRED - the end points Q(-238.5, 0) and P(228.5, 0) are printed only in the drawing. Page idx 20.
questions._flag: The drawing's end points, Q(-238.5, 0) and P(228.5, 0), are rounded and are not exact zeros of the printed p(x): p(x) = 0 gives x^2 + 10x - 54400 = 0, so x = -5 +/- sqrt(54425), about 228.29 and -238.29.
